wrong_idea: PED is the slope of the demand curve.
correction: Slope uses absolute changes; PED uses percentage changes, so it varies along a straight-line demand curve.

wrong_idea: Divide the change in price by the change in quantity.
correction: Quantity goes on top: % change in quantity demanded divided by % change in price.

wrong_idea: An elastic good has a PED below 1.
correction: Ignoring the sign, elastic means greater than 1: quantity changes proportionally more than price.

wrong_idea: Supply is equally elastic in the short and long run.
correction: Supply is usually more elastic in the long run because firms can change all their inputs.

wrong_idea: PES is usually negative like PED.
correction: PES is usually positive because a higher price leads firms to supply more.

wrong_idea: YED uses the change in price.
correction: YED uses the change in income; the good's own price is held constant.

wrong_idea: An indirect tax shifts the demand curve.
correction: The tax is paid by firms, so it raises their costs and shifts supply, not demand.

wrong_idea: Producers always pay the whole tax because they hand it to the government.
correction: Who hands the money over does not decide who bears it; the split depends on elasticities.

wrong_idea: A tax always removes the externality completely.
correction: It reduces output towards the optimum, but only fully if the tax equals the marginal external cost.
